name: Office Recent Files
location: NTUSER.DAT: Software\Microsoft\Office\<Version>\<AppName>\File MRU (Version: 10.0=OfficeXP, 11.0=Office2003, 12.0=Office2007, 14.0=Office2010, 15.0=Office2013, 16.0=Office2016/2019/M365) ; Microsoft 365 also under \User MRU\LiveId_####\File MRU (Microsoft account sign-in) and \User MRU\AD_####\File MRU (Azure AD sign-in)
purpose: Each Office application maintains its own recently-opened-files list, separate from the OS-level RecentDocs registry key and the Windows Recent Items shell folder.
key_fields: Item # value names - numbered entries, most recent typically Item 1
Value data - full file path of the opened document plus a last-opened timestamp encoded in the string
LiveId_#### / AD_#### subkeys - separate per-account File MRU lists on Microsoft 365 installs signed in with a Microsoft account or Azure AD identity
normal_baseline: Entries matching documents the user has genuinely worked on recently, with full paths in expected profile/project locations and last-opened times consistent with the user's normal working pattern.
anomalies: Full path referencing a Temp, Downloads, or email-attachment-cache directory rather than a normal document location
A document opened via a specific Office application per this key with no corresponding Trust Records or Reading Locations entry where one would be expected
File MRU entries under a LiveId_#### or AD_#### subkey for an account the primary user does not recognize signing into that Office installation
A last-opened timestamp for a file that no longer exists anywhere on disk with no other legitimate explanation for its deletion
anti_forensic_notes: Because full path and a last-opened time are recorded directly in the value data (unlike the OS RecentDocs key, which requires MRUListEx ordering to establish sequence), this list is comparatively easy to read but just as easy to clear wholesale by deleting the File MRU subkey - removing the entire per-application history at once rather than one entry at a time.
interpretation: Unlike the general RecentDocs registry key, each Office application's File MRU stores the complete file path and an explicit last-opened time per entry rather than relying on binary MRUListEx ordering, making it a more directly readable and often more precise source for reconstructing when a specific document was opened in a specific Office application. On Microsoft 365 installs, checking the correct account-specific subkey (LiveId_#### vs AD_####) matters, since separate signed-in identities keep independent lists.
